persons.name: Dhana
persons.evidence: pāsā bhājudhaṇ dvānyā bhājudhaṃ dvānyā bhājudhaṃ jamādāra strīpuruṣaṃ

notes: The era is not stated in the verse. NS is inferred from the appended 'saṃvat 973' and the Newari script. The chronogram rāma(3)-adri(7)-vivara(9), read right to left, gives 973, which matches the appended entry. 'pauṣaśukle kṣapākare' means Pauṣa śukla on a Monday (kṣapākara = moon). The scribe is Śrīnidhideva ('-ka' is a diminutive suffix and 'dvija' his brahmin status), which agrees with the catalogue. The appended Newari line ('saṃvat 973 kārttika vadi 11 śrīdattareva gayāśrāddha ṣaḍdina pāsā bhājudhaṇ dvānyā bhājudhaṃ dvānyā bhājudhaṃ jamādāra strīpuruṣaṃ luja') looks like a separate later record of a six-day Gayā-śrāddha. It apparently involves Dattareva(?) and companions ('pāsā'), including bhāju Dhana and a jamādāra couple ('strīpuruṣa'). The text is repetitive (probably dittography) and only partly understood, so the persons from this line have unclear roles and are not connected with the copying. If Kārttika vadi 11 is taken in the amānta reckoning, it would fall before the NS year-change. So the note's year may be counted differently, or it was written about a year after the copy.
